key_insight: LIGHT leverages a diffusion-forcing strategy where guidance naturally emerges from the denoising schedule itself, enabling realistic human-object interaction animations without relying on external classifiers or hand-crafted contact priors.
problem_solved: Generates believable HOI animations that jointly model dynamic human motion and diverse object geometries, removing dependence on brittle, manually designed contact priors or kinematic constraints that limit realism and generalization.
method: Frame HOI animation as a conditional diffusion process over human motion + object geometry.
Introduce diffusion forcing: use the denoising pace as intrinsic guidance (classifier-free) to encourage plausible contact and interaction dynamics.
Train end-to-end on paired human-object motion data so contact behaviors and object-specific responses are learned data‑driven rather than engineered.
impact: Reduces manual engineering and domain-specific priors for HOI synthesis, making it easier to produce diverse, realistic interaction animations that generalize across objects and actions — useful for animation, VR, robotics, and simulation pipelines.
visual_elements: Side-by-side animation strip: baseline (with hand-crafted priors) vs. LIGHT output highlighting improved contact quality.
Flowchart of the diffusion-forcing pipeline showing inputs (human + object), denoising schedule as guidance, and generated motion.
Contact overlay heatmaps across frames to visualize where and when contacts form and how LIGHT improves precision.
Bar chart comparing quantitative metrics (contact accuracy, motion realism, temporal consistency) between LIGHT and prior methods.
paper_title: Unleashing Guidance Without Classifiers for Human-Object Interaction Animation
paper_authors: Ziyin Wang, Sirui Xu, Chuan Guo, Bing Zhou, Jiangshan Gong
